author: WP19
summary: Argues that structural discipline (registry invariants, containment, link closures, generated inventories, mutation and engagement checks) must itself be tested, and gives a gate-quality checklist. The site had the policy-test table and the link-closure caveat; the three-direction registry check, containment audits, the C API inventory scope gap, the mutation and self-test gates, the five automation states and the checklist are new on the test-populations deep dive.

sections.heading: Link closures make module boundaries observable
Can a green test go red?

concepts.text: Many regressions would compile and render a plausible frame while violating a dependency, selection, ABI or evidence contract, so CNA keeps structural checks (generated-set comparisons, forbidden-token scans, link-closure probes, schemas, release criteria, engagement gates, mutation checks) beside behavioural tests.

Renderer selection is checked in three directions: the canonical CMake table, the public C++ enum and the runtime registry and descriptors, following each identity to the accessor that must return its descriptor, plus the counts stated in documents.
tokens: Renderer selection is checked in three directions at once

concepts.text: Multi-renderer builds add uniqueness, membership, default and early-selection checks; platform and audio selection have independent tables, and negative configure tests prove that host-inadmissible or mixed-SDL tuples fail with a useful diagnostic.

Native-platform containment gates scan source and link closures so a direct SDL dependency cannot reappear in SDL-free builds; hot-path and non-production audits distinguish calls allowed in adapters or tests from calls forbidden in the framework loop, with per-file ceilings that only ratchet down.
These gates prove structure; the live compositor and desktop suites still prove behaviour separately.
tokens: They prove structure; the live suites still prove behaviour

concepts.section: Link closures make module boundaries observable
concepts.text: Fifteen minimal consumers link public module aliases and a companion gate reads each generated link line, rejecting forbidden libraries and optionally requiring expected ones (math must not acquire graphics, SDL, ENet or a renderer just because an umbrella links); compile proves usability, link inspection proves dependency direction, and SDL-free and C API consumers apply the same idea at larger boundaries.
tokens: inspects the probe's generated link line for forbidden and required inputs

concepts.section: Link closures make module boundaries observable
concepts.text: The closure gate exits 77 when the generator writes no link.txt, which is honest but weaker evidence; a report records the generator and the skip state.
concepts.note: Known Issues B6 publishes the resulting permanent skip as NEW-B6-01 (CNA-BUG-032).

concepts.text: Important totals are generated: the XNA runtime audit (331 types, 3,627 members with semantic categories), Content Pipeline inventories, the C API declaration/export/ABI/coverage/limitation/consumer/release records, renderer/platform/audio set comparisons and CNB/XNB container checks.

A generated record is not automatically trustworthy: the C API coverage generator's scope table has no entry for the design, diagnostics and inspector modules and its validation refuses an unclassified module, so the checked-in coverage and not-ready release verdict describe a model that no longer covers every module; a reproduced failure outranks a checked-in percentage.

concepts.note: Known Issues B9 verifies CNA-BUG-062; the page states it as a scoped fact.

concepts.section: Can a green test go red?
concepts.text: Mutation-style checks ask whether an oracle notices its defect: Direct2D keeps pinned source mutations and log-parser positive and negative fixtures, pixel suites keep control scenes whose output changes under a perturbation, and browser drivers fail on console exceptions and require a named verdict.

concepts.section: Can a green test go red?
concepts.text: A dry-run mutation only proves the edit anchors exist; a real campaign applies each change, rebuilds, observes the expected failure and restores the source, and a log gate proves engagement only when its positive marker and negative fixtures are exercised (as DirectX11_DxvkGate does for the DXVK wrapper).
tokens: A dry run proves the wiring, not that any mutation was killed

concepts.text: TARGET has 20 workflow files; all expose manual dispatch and 18 also have push or pull-request triggers (17 on the main lines plus the content-pipeline branch); workflow presence is executable intent, a named run with artifacts is execution evidence.

Keep distinct: a script exists, CTest can register it, a workflow references it, the workflow triggered with the required environment, and the intended implementation engaged, the last often shown only by a renderer token, browser structure, native handle, validation marker or translated-API log.
tokens: Five states between a script and evidence

target.evidence: framing with three CNA instances on the page

concepts.text: A trustworthy gate states one reviewable invariant, refuses missing or empty inputs, has positive and negative fixtures, records its configuration, is wired into the intended automation, makes skips explicit and changes its parser scope with the modules it checks; a green result that was never produced is worse than a red one.
tokens: a green result that was never produced is worse than a red one

issues.text: The Direct2D mutation checker runs only as --dry-run (anchor check) in the manual d3d-windows-ci workflow; the full apply/rebuild/expect-failure run is never automated.
